# Translate, enforce terminology, publish

Translate content, enforce terminology, and round-trip the result back into its
original format with the local `kapi` CLI. For ongoing work, bind the locales,

**A single file you just need translated** — a document, a deck, one catalog —

<name>` when it needs a model provider. That's the whole task for a one-off file.

Materialize target-language files for a project, or apply bilingual files
returned by a translator back onto the project's source locales.

With no -i in a project, merge writes the target-language files from the
project block store: a process-only "kapi run" (in a project, no -o)
commits its work as targets/<locale> overlays, and merge is the matching
sink — it reads each source, applies the stored overlays, and writes the
target-language file via the source format's skeleton round-trip.

With -i, merge applies one or more bilingual files returned by a
translator back onto the project's source locales, using the skeleton
captured by kapi extract. Each input carries the extraction
batch id in a file-level <note>, so merge finds the right extraction
manifest without guessing from the filename. Mixed target locales in one
batch are fine — merge handles each input independently.

Usage:
  kapi merge [flags]

Examples:
  kapi merge                     # materialize target-language files from the project store
  kapi merge -i out/app.en-to-fr.xliff
  kapi merge -i file1.xliff -i file2.xliff
  kapi merge -i vendor-return/ --no-memory-update
  kapi merge work.kpz -o out/    # emit tar

events.text:
Done. The app is internationalized with **gen_l10n** (the Flutter-docs default, ICU-complete, typed — T2 in its recommended config) and translated to German, with the ship gate green.

**Setup**
- `l10n.yaml` — `arb-dir: lib/l10n`, template `app_en.arb`, output `app_localizations.dart`, plus `untranslated-messages-file: build/untranslated.json` (the machine-readable per-locale gap report).
- `pubspec.yaml` — `flutter: generate: true` so codegen runs on every `flutter run`/`build`; added `intl`. Generation goes into the source tree (no synthetic `package:flutter_gen`, removed around Flutter 3.29–3.32).
- `lib/l10n/app_en.arb` — the one UI string as `signInTitle`, with a `@signInTitle` description for translator context.
- `lib/l10n/l10n_ext.dart` — the standard `context.l10n` extension, so call sites stay readable instead of `AppLocalizations.of(context)!`.
- `lib/main.dart` — delegates and `supportedLocales` wired from `AppLocalizations`; the literal became `Text(c.l10n.signInTitle)`. The text moved into its own small widget because it needs a `BuildContext` below `MaterialApp`.

**Translation** — `.kapi` project (`kapi.yaml`, source `en`, target `de`) mapping `app_en.arb` → `app_{lang}.arb`, then the round-trip: pseudo-translate pre-flight → `kapi extract` → I filled the XLIFF target → `kapi merge`. `kapi check --ship` passes (QA gate, 0 findings, exit 0); `kapi status` shows `de` at 100% translated.

> "Sign in to your workspace" → **"Bei Ihrem Workspace anmelden"**

Two judgement calls worth your eye:
- **"Workspace" kept untranslated** — the dominant convention in German SaaS UIs (Slack, Notion, Figma). "Arbeitsbereich" is the alternative if you prefer fully-German product vocabulary. No terms store was bound, so nothing decided this for me; say the word and I'll re-run the round-trip and seed a terms entry so it stays consistent.
- **Formal register (Sie)** — the safe default for a business app.

I also dropped `@@locale` from the template ARB. The round-trip copies the source skeleton verbatim, so `@@locale: "en"` was landing inside `app_de.arb`, and gen_l10n hard-errors when that conflicts with the filename. Filenames are now the single source of truth, which removes the problem for every future locale rather than needing a post-edit each time.

**Not verified, and why:** there's no Flutter SDK in this environment, so I could not run codegen or render the app — the rendering check is the real gate, and it's still outstanding on your side:

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter gen-l10n     # writes lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart
flutter run                             # then set device language to German,
                                        # or MaterialApp(locale: Locale('de')) for a quick check
```

Until `flutter gen-l10n` runs, the `l10n/app_localizations.dart` import has nothing to resolve to — that's expected, not a missing step.

Done. The app is internationalized with Flutter's standard `gen_l10n` (ARB) pipeline and translated to German.

**What changed**

- `pubspec.yaml` — added `intl` and `flutter: generate: true` so `flutter gen-l10n` runs automatically on `flutter run`/`flutter build`.
- `l10n.yaml` (new) — points the generator at `lib/l10n`, template `app_en.arb`, class `AppLocalizations`.
- `lib/l10n/app_en.arb` (new) — source of truth: `signInTitle` with a `description` giving translators the screen context.
- `lib/l10n/app_de.arb` (new) — `"Bei Ihrem Workspace anmelden"`. Infinitive heading form (the German UI convention for screen titles, rather than a literal imperative "Melden Sie sich an…"), formal `Ihrem`, and `Workspace` kept as the loanword that German SaaS products use.
- `lib/main.dart` — wires up `AppLocalizations.localizationsDelegates` and `supportedLocales`, and pulls the string from the lookup. The `Scaffold` moved into a new `SignInScreen` widget because `AppLocalizations.of(context)` needs a context *below* the `MaterialApp` that provides it — reading it in `App.build` would return null.

The delegate list also brings in `GlobalMaterialLocalizations`/`Cupertino`/`Widgets`, so built-in Flutter widget strings (dialogs, date pickers, tooltips) are German too, and text direction follows the locale.

**One thing to know:** no Flutter SDK is installed in this environment, so I couldn't run `flutter gen-l10n` or compile. I hand-wrote `lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart` + the `_en`/`_de` variants in exactly the shape the generator emits, so the app compiles as-is; your first build will regenerate them in place from the ARB files. Worth running `flutter pub get && flutter gen-l10n && flutter analyze` to confirm on your SDK version. Going forward, edit only the `.arb` files — the three `.dart` files under `lib/l10n/` are generated output and are safe to gitignore if you prefer not to track them.
